title: Silence in an archive
bodyMd:
An archivist examining a fictional factory’s records found many reports of machine breakdowns but almost no accounts of routine maintenance. A visitor concluded that the factory had neglected maintenance. The archivist cautioned that the filing rules required a formal report for every breakdown, while routine maintenance was usually noted on temporary workshop cards that were discarded after a month.

This did not prove that maintenance had been adequate. It showed only that the surviving documents were produced and preserved under unequal rules. The archivist searched for other evidence, including purchase records for replacement parts and interviews with former workers. These sources had limitations of their own, but agreement or conflict between them could reveal more than the absence of a particular kind of report. An archive, she explained, records the practices of keeping evidence as well as the events themselves.
